text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Qantas chairman and former Olympics boss Gary Pemberton is to chair a new TAB board that will guide the gaming agency into its 1998 stock-market listing. The NSW Government set a timetable for the float of the TAB yesterday and the new board includes only two existing board members. Page 37.

Kerry Packer is "sitting on a $1 billion war chest" after Conpress International NV, a company owned by Packer and associated with Consolidated Press, sold its 50.3 per cent share in US communications giant Valassis Communications Inc. Shares in the compny were sold at $US24 each and Packer sold 20.2 million shares, giving him a net gain of $US484 million. Page 37.

Newcrest mining shares feel to an all-time low of $A2.20 yesterday after its foray into Normandy Mining wreaked havoc with the companies shareholders. The shares hit the low as rumours of a close call with the ANZ Bank over a gold loan deal hit the stock xchange, and share prices still closed at a low of $A2.40 after the company clarified its position. Page 38.

Australia's biggest gold producer Normandy Mining Ltd will survive the current downfall in gold prices because it has a hedged portfolio that can sustain four years production at the rate of 1.51 million ounces, and as a result of four consecutive years of falling cash production costs. Page 38.

New drilling techniques designed to minimise hole formation damage has allowed Santos Ltd to make one of the biggest onshore gas discoveries in more than two decades, at the south-west Qld Beeree 1 wildcat well. The well is 50km north of the Ballera gas cntre in Qld and the new discovery can be used to supply the increasing gas demand in NSW and Qld. Page 41.

Pension mis-selling in the UK goes back to the late 1980s when the Conservative Government encouraged people to move to private pension schemes and many were advised badly. In the latest saga the economic secretary to the Treasurer in Britain, Helen Liddel, has named Australian-owned companies Colonial and AMP's Pearl as among the worst in compensating people for pension mis-selling. Page 42.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Reserve Bank governor Ian McLachlan yesterday defended the bank's decision to sell two-thirds of its gold reserves claiming the decision will save taxpayers $150 million a year. McLachlan further accused the gold industry of being largely responsible forthe recent plunge in global gold markets by exaggerating the impact of the bank's decision. Page 1.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported yesterday that the economy had lost 16,900 full-time jobs in June. The financial market reacted badly to the news driving the Australian dollar to a new 18-month low and renewing calls for a cut in interest raes. Page 19.

Giant food group Goodman Fielder have confirmed that Australian Federal Police raided its Sydney headquarters in late June. The raid was part of an investigation into alleged irregularities involving the Federal Government's export market development grats scheme. Page 19

Australia's largest supermarket chain, Woolworths, yesterday posted a record sales figure for the year ending June 29 of $A15.57 billion. The result has been hailed as a sign of recovery in the beleaguered retail sector. Page 19.

Australian Pharmaceutical Industries (API) yesterday announced record revenue and profits for its first year as a listed company. API said that net profits rose to $A23.9 million in the year to April 30, a result of a 15.1 per cent increase in revenue to$A855.5 million. Page 20.

The Federal Court has appointed a receiver and manager to New South Wales-based United Tree Farmers following the company's failure to obey a court order issued last month to amend its fund-raising activities. The Federal Court had instructed United TreeFarmers to provide the Australian Securities Commission with a prospectus and trust deed and to nominate an independent trustee, all specified regulations under Corporation Law. Page 20.

Australian wine company Southcorp is preparing to expand its international wine business as part of a strategy aimed at consolidating its position as the world's premier producer of top reds and to spread climactic risk. Southcorp chief executive Graham Kraehe yesterday refused to reveal what overseas assets had been acquired but said an announcement would be made within the month. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Executive chairman of Normandy Mining Robert Champion de Crespigny conceded yesterday that the gold industry asked for the latest involvement in the industry by the Reserve Bank by not effectively being able to lobby and communicate their needs to the government. He says there is a dilemma in knowing how to communicate demands for assistance without receiving the kind of interference the industry has seen recently. Page 25.

A working group of State and Federal bureaucrats has been set up to settle a row between their respective Government's, after no agreement was reached on whether the States would pay the Federal Government's new superannuation surcharge. The Federal Goverment faces a $A250 million hole in the new tax because of the lack of State support and as a result of a drafting error that will exempt wealthy people and politicians from paying the tax. Page 25.

Price Waterhouse's New York-based retailing expert Herb Kleinberger has found Australian retail stores lack ambience and are dowdy, with Australian shop keepers being uninterested, fashion colours dull and sizes out of date. He found Australia to be far ehind the US and Europe in retailing concepts. Page 29.

Sources close to the sale of Imperial Chemical Industries plc's controlling stake in ICI Australia have revealed the bidding range by institutions for shares in ICI is between $A12.25 and $A12.65, giving Imperial at least a $A1.2 billion profit from the sle. Page 27.

President and chief executive of McDonald's USA, Edward Rensi, has announced his retirement as the hamburger giant faces sagging US sales and unhappy franchises. Rensi's retirement comes as part of a new campaign of sweeping management changes by the company to boost sales, but disgruntled franchise owners disagreed the changes would solve the real problems such as the quality of McDonald's food. Page 26.

Microsoft is struggling to find an audience for its on-line entertainment and has announced it will make more services freely available to all those using the World Wide Web. The company will switch its focus from the TV style entertainment products that ere released last year to concentrate on a more service-orientated programming. Page 26.
THE AGE

It is believed Kerry Stokes' Seven Network has bought Australia Television International from The Australian Broadcasting Corporation for $4.5 million. The deal included an agreement by Seven to include ABC news broadcasts and gives the network a ready-mae entry into the Asian satellite TV market. Page A2.

Six months of negotiations between the Victorian Government and Hong Kong-based shipping giant Orient Overseas Container Liner have failed, with Orient pulling out of a $A150 million deal designed to break the existing duopoly currently existing in the Port of Melbourne. Orient is likely to take its investment to Sydney, threatening the Vic Government's attempts to reform the Port of Melbourne and Melbourne's position as Australia's shipping hub. Page B1.

A management shake-up at Apple Computer APPL.O has resulted from the resignation of chief executive and chairman Gilbert Amelio after just 17 months. Apple's co-founder Steve Jobs will now have an expanded role in the company and will try to pull it out of a slmp that has seen management defections and a string of resignations. Page B2.

Managing director of the ANZ's investment banking arm, John Sunderland, believes the unit is heading for increased profits and higher revenue in the year ahead. He says the increase will come as the Bank's fee revenue rises as a result of its new role as dviser, arranger and distributor on international deals. Page B3.

Geelong football club is hoping star player Gary Ablett will retire from playing the game this week and accept an offer of an ambassadorial role to salvage his reputation. Ablett has been leading a hectic life style after his commitment to football and te church dwindled and he is set to lose a marketing contract with Club 10 after failing to turn up to a promotion in Sydney on Wednesday. Page A1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has cooled expectations of further interest rate cuts by announcing the last four easings were yet to impact on the economy. Market hopes for another rate cut were high because of figures released yesterday showing employent figures to be worse than expected. Page B1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
